description.value: The study investigated associations between clinical and cognitive insight and brain activation and task-related connectivity during emotion regulation in individuals with schizophrenia.

spans.text: We investigated the association between insight and brain activation and connectivity during emotion regulation.

value: We hypothesize that patients with impaired insight are less able to regulate their negative emotions through reappraisal and will make more use of suppression.

We hypothesize that patients with poorer cognitive insight show increased activation of prefrontal and emotional arousal-related areas, as well as more connectivity between prefrontal and emotional arousal-related areas suggesting increased mental effort and top-down control to exert cognitive reappraisal.

We hypothesize that patients with poorer clinical insight will make more use of suppression and, therefore, will show less brain activation of and connectivity between relevant areas (DLPFC, VLPF and insula) during suppression compared to patients with better insight.

name.value: Schedule for the Assessment of Insight – Expanded

spans.text: Schedule for the Assessment of Insight – Expanded (SAI-E)
The SAI-E is a 12-item researcher-reported semi-structured interview measuring three subdimensions of insight

description.value: The Schedule for the Assessment of Insight–Expanded (SAI-E) was a 12-item researcher-reported semi-structured interview used to measure clinical insight in patients with schizophrenia. It assessed awareness of illness, relabeling of symptoms, and awareness of need for treatment; subscale scores and a subtotal score were used in fMRI analyses, with higher scores indicating better clinical insight.

spans.text: The SAI-E is a 12-item researcher-reported semi-structured interview measuring three subdimensions of insight: (1) awareness of illness, (2) relabeling of symptoms and (3) awareness of need for treatment
Beck Cognitive Insight Scale (BCIS)
The BCIS is a self-report 15-item questionnaire that consists of two subscales

description.value: The Beck Cognitive Insight Scale (BCIS) was a 15-item self-report questionnaire used to measure cognitive insight in patients with schizophrenia. It produced self-reflection and self-certainty subscale scores and a composite index calculated as self-reflection minus self-certainty; all three scores were used in fMRI analyses.

spans.text: The BCIS is a self-report 15-item questionnaire that consists of two subscales: (1) self-reflection (SR; e.g., ‘I am sometimes wrong about how people feel and think about me’; 9 items) and (2) self-certainty (SC; e.g., ‘my interpretations of my experiences are absolutely right’; 6 items).

At first level, a general linear model (GLM) was created which included 14 condition-regressors (7 condition-regressors per session) modelled with a boxcar function convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function (HRF): (1) view, (2) attend neutral, (3) attend negative, (4) reappraisal, (5) suppression, (6) increase, (7) after.

model_settings.value: Second-level whole-brain random-effects multiple regression in 30 patients using reappraisal > attend negative or suppression > attend negative contrasts and demeaned SAI-E insight scores as covariates; initial voxel threshold p < 0.001 uncorrected and cluster-level FWE correction at p < 0.05. First-level models used boxcar regressors convolved with a canonical HRF, six motion parameters and derivatives, a 128 s high-pass filter, and AR(1) serial-correlation modeling.
